title: Vis2Reg: Visibility-Aware Landmark-Free Geometric 3D--2D Registration for Liver Laparoscopy
summary: Accurate 3D--2D liver registration, which aligns preoperative 3D models to partial, view-dependent intraoperative surface observations, is critical for AR-guided laparoscopic surgery but remains challenging due to severe occlusion, limited visibility, and the lack of 3D ground-truth supervision. Existing landmark-free approaches perform partial-to-complete geometric alignment, yet robust self-supervision under extreme partial visibility remains difficult. We propose Vis2Reg, a visibility-aware registration framework that explicitly constrains deformation using mask-consistent visible regions. We introduce a visibility-aware self-supervision that derives a visible-domain 3D supervision signal from intraoperative masks, enabled by differentiable point rasterization and mask-guided back-projection. This formulation improves robustness under severe occlusion while maintaining fully self-supervised learning. Vis2Reg combines a robust geometric rigid initialization module with an implicit neural deformation field for stable alignment. Vis2Reg achieves a Dice score of 92.6\% and a Chamfer Distance of 1.43 mm on real intraoperative datasets, with 111 ms per-frame inference time, demonstrating both accuracy and practical efficiency.
tldr: Vis2Reg introduces a visibility-aware self-supervised framework for 3D-2D liver registration during laparoscopy, using mask-guided differentiable rasterization to handle severe occlusion and achieve high accuracy (92.6% Dice, 1.43 mm Chamfer) with real-time inference (111 ms).
tldr_zh: Vis2Reg提出了一种面向腹腔镜手术的可见性感知自监督3D-2D肝脏配准框架，利用掩码引导的可微光栅化处理严重遮挡问题，实现了高精度（Dice 92.6%，Chamfer距离1.43 mm）和实时推理（111 ms）。
summary_zh: 精准的3D-2D肝脏配准，即将术前三维模型与术中的局部、视角依赖的表面观测对齐，对于增强现实引导的腹腔镜手术至关重要，但由于严重的遮挡、有限的可见性以及缺乏三维真实标注监督，仍然面临挑战。现有的无标记点方法实现了部分到整体的几何对齐，但在极端部分可见性下的鲁棒自监督仍然困难。我们提出Vis2Reg，一种可见性感知的配准框架，通过掩膜一致的可见区域显式约束形变。我们引入了一种可见性感知的自监督方法，通过可微点光栅化和掩膜引导的反向投影，从术中掩膜中导出可见域的三维监督信号。该公式在严重遮挡下提升了鲁棒性，同时保持了完全自监督学习。Vis2Reg结合了稳健的几何刚性初始化模块与隐式神经形变场，以实现稳定的对齐。在实际术中数据集上，Vis2Reg实现了92.6%的Dice分数和1.43毫米的Chamfer距离，每帧推理时间为111毫秒，展示了准确性与实际效率。

title: Measuring and Improving Complex-Atomic Answer Consistency in Endoscopic VQA
summary: Endoscopic visual question answering (VQA) increasingly asks complex questions that combine several endoscopic answer components rather than isolated factual queries. Such complex answers may be scored as correct even when the same model fails on associated atomic questions. We introduce EndoCA, a paired complex-atomic answer consistency benchmark for evaluating whether complex answers remain consistent with same-image atomic answers. EndoCA contains two suites: EndoCA-Core evaluates compact question-complexity patterns commonly seen in practical endoscopic VQA, and EndoCA-Diagnostic supports controlled analysis across increasing question complexity. We evaluate 11 VLMs spanning open, medical, endoscopy-adapted, and closed-source models on EndoCA. Some VLMs achieve high complex-answer accuracy, yet their atomic-answer accuracy and complex-atomic answer consistency remain substantially lower. To reduce this complex-atomic inconsistency, we introduce Atomic-Support Reconciliation (ASR), a training-free mechanism that uses model-generated atomic answers as contextual premises for answer revision and consistency-guided selective answering. On four selected publicly available models, ASR-Revise improves paired complex-atomic correctness with modest changes in complex-answer accuracy, while ASR-Selective improves accuracy on answered cases by allowing the model to abstain from less reliable cases. Together, EndoCA and ASR provide a consistency-aware benchmark and a training-free mechanism for answer reconciliation and selective answering in endoscopic VQA.
tldr: The paper introduces EndoCA, a benchmark to evaluate complex-atomic answer consistency in endoscopic VQA, and proposes ASR, a training-free mechanism to improve consistency by using atomic answers as premises for revision or abstention.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了EndoCA基准，用于评估内窥镜VQA中的复杂-原子答案一致性，并提出了ASR，一种利用原子答案作为前提进行答案修订或选择性回答的无训练机制。
summary_zh:
摘要：  
内窥镜视觉问答（VQA）日益关注结合多个内窥镜答案组件的复杂问题，而非孤立的事实性查询。即便同一模型在相关原子问题上失败，此类复杂答案仍可能被判定为正确。我们提出EndoCA——一个配对复杂-原子答案一致性基准，用于评估复杂答案是否与同一图像的原子答案保持一致。EndoCA包含两个套件：EndoCA-Core评估实际内窥镜VQA中常见的紧凑型问题复杂度模式；EndoCA-Diagnostic支持跨递增问题复杂度的受控分析。我们在EndoCA上评估了11种视觉语言模型（VLM），涵盖开源、医学、内窥镜适配及闭源模型。部分VLM在复杂答案准确率上表现优异，但其原子答案准确率及复杂-原子答案一致性仍显著偏低。为降低这种复杂-原子不一致性，我们提出原子支持调和（ASR）——一种无需训练的机制，利用模型生成的原子答案作为答案修正的上下文前提，以及一致性引导的选择性回答。在四个选定的公开可用模型上，ASR-修正以微小的复杂答案准确率变化提升了配对复杂-原子正确性；ASR-选择性则通过允许模型放弃可靠性较低的情况，提升了已回答案例的准确率。EndoCA与ASR共同为内窥镜VQA中的答案调和与选择性回答提供了一种一致性感知基准和无需训练的机制。

title: Memory-Supported Synergistic Adaptation for Training-Free Test-Time Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Test-time adaptation (TTA) aims to mitigate distribution shifts by adapting models with unlabeled target data at inference time. While TTA with vision-language models (VLMs) has shown promising results in classification, extending it to medical image segmentation remains challenging. In this setting, the adaptation gains from optimizing on VLM-generated predictions are often outweighed by the degradation to the VLM's strong pretrained features caused by noisy, update-driven learning, resulting in limited and unstable improvements. We therefore propose Memory-Supported Synergistic Adaptation (MSSA), a novel training-free TTA framework for medical image segmentation. Without updating model parameters, MSSA dynamically selects reliable image-text predictions to construct an online memory, uses them as text-guided semantic priors, and couples them with cross-image structural alignment for robust adaptation. Specifically, MSSA consists of (i) a noise-aware memory construction module that filters and stabilizes cross-modal predictions, and (ii) a relevance-driven prototype alignment module that aligns the target sample with structurally consistent memory samples and their reliable predictions to improve adaptation. Extensive experiments on multiple medical segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that MSSA consistently improves VLM-based segmentation models and outperforms existing fine-tuning-based TTA methods by a clear margin, with gains of up to 12.2% DSC and 11.7% mIoU. Project page: https://lingrayy.github.io/MSSA/ .
tldr: This paper introduces MSSA, a training-free test-time adaptation framework for medical image segmentation that dynamically constructs an online memory from reliable image-text predictions and aligns prototypes across images to improve Vision-Language Model (VLM) performance without parameter updates, outperforming fine-tuning methods by up to 12.2% DSC on benchmarks.
tldr_zh: 本文提出MSSA，一种无需训练的测试时自适应框架，用于医学图像分割。它通过动态构建在线记忆库存储可靠的图像-文本预测，并跨图像对齐原型来提升视觉语言模型（VLM）性能，无需更新参数，在基准测试上比微调方法高出多达12.2%的DSC。
summary_zh: 测试时自适应（TTA）旨在通过推理阶段利用无标注目标数据适配模型来缓解分布偏移。尽管基于视觉-语言模型（VLM）的TTA在分类任务中取得了良好效果，但将其扩展至医学图像分割仍面临挑战。在此场景下，通过优化VLM生成预测所获得的适配增益，往往被因噪声干扰的更新驱动学习导致的VLM强预训练特征退化所抵消，最终导致改进效果有限且不稳定。为此，我们提出记忆支持协同适配（MSSA），一种新型无需训练的医学图像分割TTA框架。在不更新模型参数的情况下，MSSA动态筛选可靠的图像-文本预测以构建在线记忆，将其作为文本引导的语义先验，并结合跨图像结构对齐实现鲁棒适配。具体而言，MSSA包含：(i) 噪声感知记忆构建模块，用于过滤和稳定跨模态预测；(ii) 相关性驱动原型对齐模块，将目标样本与结构一致的记忆样本及其可靠预测对齐以提升适配效果。在多个医学分割基准上的大量实验表明，MSSA能持续提升基于VLM的分割模型性能，并以高达12.2% DSC和11.7% mIoU的增益明显优于现有基于微调的TTA方法。项目页面：https://lingrayy.github.io/MSSA/。
